title: How to Convert Your HEW 6 Salary to Annual Pay: Hourly Rate, Fortnight, Tax and Super
description: Learn how to convert a HEW 6 salary hourly rate to annual, fortnightly and weekly pay using a 38-hour week. Includes tax, super and minimum wage comparisons.
salarySummary: For a HEW 6 salary, multiply the hourly rate by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks to get annual gross pay, then add 12% super on top.

faqs.q: What is the HEW 6 salary hourly rate?
faqs.a: The HEW 6 classification is defined in the Higher Education Industry Award. The exact hourly rate depends on your employer and any applicable enterprise agreement. You can find the correct rate using the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay Calculator or by checking your award. Once you have the hourly rate, use the formula: hourly × 38 × 52 to estimate annual pay.

faqs.q: Does the HEW 6 salary include casual loading?
faqs.a: No. Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate for casual employees. If you are a casual HEW 6 employee, your employer should pay the base rate plus 25% loading. When using our timesheet, select the checkbox for casual loading only if you are paid the base rate and want to see the loaded rate. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

faqs.q: How is super calculated on a HEW 6 salary?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay. For a HEW 6 salary, super is calculated on your base hourly rate (or casual rate if applicable) and is not deducted from your take-home pay. The maximum contribution base for super in 2026–27 is $270,830. Our calculator estimates super at 12% of ordinary earnings.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your HEW 6 Salary: From Hourly to Annual

If you’re offered a **HEW 6 salary** or you’re an existing employee wanting to compare your hourly rate to an annual figure, the conversion is straightforward. The key is knowing your base hourly rate and the standard full-time hours. For most awards, including the Higher Education Industry Award that covers HEW 6 roles, the ordinary hours are 38 per week. This article explains how to convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly and weekly pay, and what to consider for tax and super.

## How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay

The basic formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates or allowances. For a full-time HEW 6 employee on 38 hours per week, the calculation is:

Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52

For example, if your HEW 6 hourly rate is $40.00, your annual gross pay would be $40.00 × 38 × 52 = $79,040.

### The 38-Hour Week

The standard full-time week in Australia is 38 ordinary hours, as set by the Fair Work Act and the National Employment Standards. This is the basis for the National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) and most award rates. When you use our [the timesheet](/), we assume 38 hours per week unless you change it. Always check your award or agreement – some may have different ordinary hours (e.g., 35 or 40 hours).

### The Fortnight

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the example above:

Weekly pay = $40.00 × 38 = $1,520.00
Fortnightly pay = $1,520.00 × 2 = $3,040.00

Knowing your fortnightly amount helps you budget and compare with job advertisements that quote fortnightly salaries.

## Tax and Super on Your HEW 6 Salary

### Income Tax (2026–27 Resident Rates)

Tax is deducted from your gross pay. The 2026–27 tax rates for residents are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners). Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator applies these rates to estimate your net pay after tax and Medicare.

### Superannuation Guarantee

Your employer must pay super guarantee of 12% on your ordinary earnings, on top of your gross pay. This means if your annual gross is $79,040, your employer contributes an additional $9,484.80 to your super fund (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830). Super is not deducted from your take-home pay – it’s an extra benefit. Learn more on our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

## Understanding Different Pay Types

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour) is the minimum for award/agreement-free employees. Most HEW 6 employees are covered by the Higher Education Industry Award, which sets higher minimum rates. Always check your award or enterprise agreement. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) and a Pay Calculator to find your correct rate.

### Casual Loading

If you are a casual HEW 6 employee, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave. When using our [the timesheet](/), select the casual loading checkbox only if you want to see the loaded rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading – the tool adds it for you. For more details, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) topic.

### Annualised Wages and Salaries

Some employers offer an annualised wage or salary that covers penalties, overtime and allowances. This is common in enterprise agreements. If your HEW 6 salary is an annualised amount, you must ensure it is at least what you would earn under the award for all hours worked. The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that annualised wages must be reviewed every 12 months. Our conversion tool assumes a simple hourly rate without these extras – use it as a starting point.

## HEW 6 Salary Example

Let’s say your HEW 6 classification has a base hourly rate of $45.00 under your enterprise agreement. Here’s how the numbers look:

- Weekly (38 hours): $45.00 × 38 = $1,710.00
- Fortnightly: $1,710.00 × 2 = $3,420.00
- Annual gross: $45.00 × 38 × 52 = $88,920.00
- Super (12%): $10,670.40 paid on top
- Estimated tax (2026–27, no HELP or surcharge): approximately $20,867 (including Medicare)
- Estimated take-home: $68,053 per year (before any salary packaging)

These figures are estimates. Your actual pay may differ due to salary sacrifice, HELP repayments, or the Medicare levy surcharge. Always consult the [reference tables](/data) on our site for the latest rates.

## Conclusion

Converting your HEW 6 salary from hourly to annual is simple: multiply by 38 and 52. Remember to add super on top and deduct tax for your net pay. Use our [the timesheet](/) to quickly calculate your weekly, fortnightly and annual figures. For award-specific rates, check the Fair Work Ombudsman’s resources. Understanding these conversions helps you compare job offers and plan your finances.

*Disclaimer: Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.*
